purpose: Targeted quote-canonicalization intervention after measured typography sensitivity and negative C tuning
quote_rule: U+2018/2019/201A/201B -> ASCII apostrophe; U+201C/201D/201E/201F -> ASCII double quote
placement: stateless quote_normalize transformer before TF-IDF inside the complete calibrated pipeline
primary_comparison: wc120_norm minus wc120_raw on identical quote_typography validation inputs
secondary_comparisons: within-representation clean and quote differences for C60; clean cost, dash axis and incumbent-relative differences
cv: three training-only stratified folds; four fixed pipelines and 12 candidate-fold fits; raw-margin AUROC on all three input conditions

export_rule.budget_note: The 0.003 point-loss budget is an exploratory preference fixed after v2 diagnosis but before v3 scores; it is not a statistical noninferiority margin. Passing only this tradeoff rule does not establish a better Kaggle model.

stopping_rule: Complete the 12 CV fits, two normalized 8000-row fits, full train-preprocessing x input-condition matrix and verification; export at most one eligible candidate. Do not add a second intervention or expand parameters in this run.
limitations: This intervention follows inspected public and development diagnostics; it is not an untouched test.
Equal normalized-model predictions on raw and canonical quotes are guaranteed by construction, not independent robustness evidence.
Dash is an additional diagnostic axis already observed in v2, not a new independent holdout.
Bootstrap intervals condition on models and this split, omitting training variation and selection adjustment.
A robustness-tradeoff candidate may slightly reduce clean performance and has no established public/private gain.
